title: Client-SLO-aware graded degradation with degraded stubs and priority prefetch admission
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional spikes and global staggered outages we see two recurring failure modes: (1) large tail latency spikes from under-provisioned KV/cache warmup and long model cold-starts, and (2) high request drop rates when token-based batching saturates GPU slots. Both cause customer-visible SLO violations and noisy retries. Existing policies focus on strict priority lanes or binary shedding; they either drop too many requests or route everything to a lower-quality fallback, losing subtlety for SLO-sensitive customers.

Goal: Implement a client-SLO-aware graded-degradation system that: (a) admits requests via a short-term priority-prefetch admission controller, (b) serves a spectrum of degraded responses (from full-generation to short ‘stub’ answers or cached summaries) with explicit provenance/confidence, and (c) couples shedding decisions to observable customer SLO budgets and multi-region failover status. The system must be pluggable into runtime admission and routing stacks and observable in Console.

Approach:
- Admission: introduce a Priority Prefetch Admission (PPA) stage before batching. PPA uses per-tenant SLO tokens (budget) and short-lived prefetch hints. Requests can be tagged as latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, or background. PPA uses a time-windowed token bucket + dynamic weight scheduler to decide admission, prefetch model KV/cache, and optionally escalate to immediate fast-path.
- Degraded responses: define graded response modes: FULL (normal generation), SNIPPET (trimmed output with deterministic extractive summarization), STUB (cached or templated response with recommended next steps), and FALLBACK_MODEL (lower-cost quantized variant). Each response includes metadata: mode, estimated confidence, and provenance URL for audit.
- Backfill & Prefetch: for admitted requests that will be delayed by batching, PPA can proactively prefetch KV cache and partial key-value context (e.g., last-turn embeddings) for high-probability candidates to reduce cold-start token costs. Prefetch budget is bounded by tenant-specific credit and global prefetch limits.
- Multi-region & circuit breaker integration: PPA reads region health and routing weights. On region degradation, requests can be admitted with a forced degradation mode or proactively redirected. Circuit breakers per-tenant will flag sustained high-drop rates and trigger escalation (notify SE and reduce admission thresholds).
- Operator control & observability: add Console controls for tenant SLO budgets, prefetch budget, and degradation policy overrides. Emit detailed traces for every admitted/dropped request: admission_decision, prefetch_decision, degradation_mode, and latency breakouts.

Why different: This combines proactive prefetching with graded stub responses driven by client SLO budgets rather than pure priority-dropping; it preserves request-level fidelity (provenance/confidence), reduces unnecessary retries, and lets product teams trade cost vs quality per tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller implements PPA algorithm and exposes per-tenant token consumption metrics.
At overload, at least 3 graded degradation modes are available and each response includes mode/confidence/provenance header.
Prefetch reduces cold-start token cost (measured) by >=20% p50 for targeted tenants in canary region under synthetic spike.
Console shows per-route degradation rate and per-tenant SLO budget consumption with alerting thresholds.
End-to-end canary demonstrates maintained customer SLO (p95 latency) for top-10 customers while overall dropped_requests reduced vs baseline by 30%.
Automated tests and chaos experiments validate that multi-region failover with forced region outage falls back to degraded-mode routing with no data leakage.
design_notes:
Algorithm sketch: maintain per-tenant sliding-window tokens (tokens grant admission to fast-path). On request arrival: check token level, request priority, and region health. If tokens available and priority high => admit to fast-path; if tokens low but prefetch budget available => admit with PREFETCH flag and schedule KV prefetch, else apply degradation policy mapping (SNIPPET/STUB/FALLBACK_MODEL). Admission scoring uses historical latencies and a small ML-based predictor (trained offline) to estimate downstream batch wait and whether prefetch helps. Prefetch should be idempotent and cancelable. All degradation decisions must attach 'x-redwood-degradation' headers for downstream routing. For safety, any STUB response must include 'why' and a link to the audit log. Testability: injection points for region health and token budgets. Costs: prefetch increases short-term bandwidth and datastore reads; counters needed to avoid runaway prefetch during broad spikes.

Trade-offs considered:
- More aggressive prefetch reduces latency but increases read costs and cache churn.
- More granular degradation modes improve UX but add surface area for correctness and telemetry.
- ML predictor improves admission but adds model maintenance; fallback deterministic heuristics included.
rollout_plan: 1) Design review and owner assignment (2 weeks). 2) Implement PPA as feature-flagged middleware in serving runtime (4 weeks). 3) Implement degradation modes and response schema + Console telemetry (3 weeks). 4) Internal canary on non-critical tenant cohort (2 weeks) measuring metrics. 5) Controlled expansion to top-10 customers with SE coordination (2 weeks). 6) Global rollout with default conservative budgets (1 week). Rollback: feature flag off disables prefetch and reverts to existing admission heuristics. Postmortem checkpoint after 3 days of global rollout.
tests: Unit tests for PPA token accounting and prefetch cancellation
Integration test: synthetic spike with prefetch on vs off measuring latency/cost
Chaos test: kill region in staging and verify multi-region fallback uses STUB/FALLBACK_MODEL per policy
Security test: ensure no sensitive data returned in STUB responses (automated content scanner)
